CONTENT: 1️⃣ Repository Identity & Discoverability
Create the Git repository and push an initial commit to GitHub
DESCRIPTION: Create the repository if it does not exist. If starting locally, run git init, add the remote origin, and push an initial README commit so issues, automation, and collaboration can be configured against a real default branch.

CONTENT: Create and add a .gitignore
DESCRIPTION: Add a .gitignore tailored to the tech stack before committing application code so build outputs, secrets, and machine-specific files are not tracked.

CONTENT: Update owner avatar to a current and recognisable image
DESCRIPTION: Check the owner or org profile image is current, clearly branded, and readable at small sizes so people can quickly recognise the repository source in search and activity feeds.

CONTENT: Choose and apply a clear, kebab-case repository name
DESCRIPTION: Use a short, specific name that states what the repository is and who it serves. Descriptive names improve search relevance, reduce ambiguity, and make project intent obvious to contributors.

CONTENT: Write a strong repository description
DESCRIPTION: Write a one-line description that clearly explains what the repository does and who it is for. A strong description improves searchability and creates a better first impression in listings and profile views.

CONTENT: Add appropriate topics to improve discoverability
Set repository scope correctly (public or private)
Pin the repository on your profile (if relevant)
DESCRIPTION: Pin the repository if it represents active or priority work you want to highlight publicly. Pinned repos improve profile clarity and help visitors quickly understand your focus areas.

CONTENT: Set the repository Watch level to the desired signal
DESCRIPTION: Choose the Watch level that matches your intent: Not watching for minimal noise, Participating for thread-level updates, or All activity for close monitoring.

CONTENT: Run the Repo Ecosystem Watch review and decide which related repos to Watch or Star
DESCRIPTION: Review adjacent repositories in the same ecosystem and assign an action for each one. Use Watch for ongoing monitoring and Star for lightweight bookmarking and future reference.

CONTENT: Star the repository and assign to the appropriate organisational list
Identify automation opportunities using GitHub Script and GitHub Actions
DESCRIPTION: Identify repetitive repository tasks that can be automated, such as issue triage, release tagging, scheduled checks, and documentation sync. Capture at least one candidate workflow with trigger, owner, and expected outcome.
